You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: How long will an O'Reilly license stay active before it is automatically revoked for an Engineering team member?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): The license is removed after three months.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[Self-Paced External Trainings > O'Reilly Learning > How to get an O'Reilly license]
O'Reilly is funded by Engineering, so is currently only available for Engineering team members please request access via [Lumos](/handbook/security/corporate/systems/lumos/ar/). Please note, seats are very limited, so you may need to wait until one becomes available.

To ensure seats and licenses are used effectively, access will be removed after 3 months to reallocate seats/licenses to other users. If you would like access again in the future, you can re-request it.

If you're outside of Engineering and would like an O'Reilly license, you can purchase one using the [G&D Fund](/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/).

[GitLab Offboarding > Offboarding Overview > Involuntary Terminations > Severance Process for US-based Team Members]
*Important Notes:*

- Separation pay is not paid until the ex-team member signs the document and the revocation period has passed.
- We treat team members equally and therefore do not take tenure into consideration when determining separation pay unless legally required. We know that other companies sometimes gives higher separation pay to longer tenure. We think that a short tenure can be harder to explain to a next employer and with a shorter tenure you might have less stock option upside, maybe you have not even reached your vesting cliff.
- Make sure you understand the rules for over 40.
- You must use language in your exit meeting that is in no way forceful of the ex-team member to sign the agreement. Use phrasing such as "if you choose to sign"; "you have a right to have legal council review this document before you sign", etc.

[GitLab Offboarding Standards > Purpose > Offboarding Procedure > Notice of Offboarding]
Once the termination process has been approved and completed in Workday either by the departing team member's [Direct Manager](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Fr1G1i1kssfADgDf3D6LbZHR8RZmWKZYDNV8AfduZ1c/edit) (Voluntary) or by [Team Member Relations](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nMokz03AiUQtb0XV5zpD9CjaQKcX5Lu8p5ASZy3cJVA/edit) (Involuntary), on the team member's Last Working Day, at the pre-determined time, the Offboarding Parent and Child Cases are created automatically in [Compass](/handbook/eta/corporate-it/compass/), if within a valid offboarding window for the specified day. All system owners receive an email notifying them of their Child Case so that access revocation can begin. In the instance of a Voluntary Termination, this process will follow the [resignation process](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AVHHBKd6dtyn0DOl4_UydbdEhectLpH5aMh17r9Sg_4/edit) initiated by the team member directly in Workday.

In alignment with the needs of both People Operations and IT Operations, scheduled offboardings will be opened between 4:00 - 5:00pm of the **team members' local timezone** in Slack Monday-Friday.

**Note:** In instances where team members require deprovisioning initiated outside of these times, team members or their manager should reach out to IT Operations to arrange an alternate time.

[GitLab Offboarding > Offboarding Overview > Involuntary Terminations > Last Working Day]
[People Engineering automations](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/peopleops-eng/employment-automation) will generate the offboarding issue at the end of the team member's last working day, as per notification from the Team Member Relations Specialist (TMR) and the People Business Partner (PBP). Once the `Last Working Day` or Garden leave expires the team member will be officially offboarded from GitLab.  Prior to the offboarding issue and the overall process for the term listed below.

[Self-Paced External Trainings > O'Reilly Learning > MasterClass]
MasterClass gives every GitLab team member access to world-class instructors across a huge range of subjects — from leadership and communication to creativity, writing, cooking, and beyond. Whether you're looking to sharpen a professional skill or explore something entirely new, MasterClass is a great place to start.

The content itself is genuinely exceptional. You'll learn directly from people who are the best in the world at what they do — think Diane von Furstenberg on building a brand, Chris Voss on negotiation, or Roxane Gay on inclusive storytelling. The production quality is second to none, and courses are broken into short, digestible lessons that fit easily into a busy schedule.

All GitLab team members have a MasterClass license included as part of our learning offering, so there's no cost and no approval needed — just log in and start learning.

[Self-Paced External Trainings > O'Reilly Learning]
The O'Reilly Learning library, contains thousands of books, videos and live learning courses to assist team members with professional development and staying up-to-date with changing technology trends. Additionally, code sandboxes are included within the O'Reilly platform that team members can utilize to practice new skills or hone existing ones.
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
Access to an O'Reilly license will be removed after 3 months to reallocate seats to other users [1].
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
